At the time, I think the commander was a person by the name of Tajtuk [phoen], and we came up with this document where we talk about something to the effect that if a conflict should occur, we would use our resources and people together in order to save everybody, regardless of who was in question, and this is very important. I don't need to read this. I mean, this is a terrible copy. So what was agreed was that an UNPROFOR transporter be available for the extraction of wounded civilians and soldiers. All problems on the side of the army and the HVO should be dispatched for resolution the same day by members of the Medical Corps and the chief of the Medical Corps of the 4th Corps. This was my colleague, Dzemal, the head of the 4th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bagaric, you initiated this?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you hear me? Did you initiate this meeting?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did. I said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's look at the next document, 3D -- 2D319. This document was also signed by you. This is an exhibit we've already seen of the 6th of May, 1993. You are appointing a surgical team to work in the Jablanica War Hospital?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Already at this time, Mr. Bagaric, on the 6th of May, because your report was from the 5th of May from the visits where you went with Mr. Petkovic, already in that section did the conflict break out between the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: On the 6th of May, 1993, after all that had happened up in Konjic, at the request of the medical or the surgical team from Jablanica, I am writing an order to the regional war hospital of the HVO in Mostar to relieve this team, so the order goes into effect immediately. We did affect this shift, this relief.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Who formed this hospital in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: The hospital in Jablanica was formed by doctors of the HVO, but we did not think about it as particularly ours, quote/unquote. The director of the medical centre at the time agreed to be the director of that institution. We treated it as one of our institutions, in terms of coverage, and we provided treatment together of both ethnic groups until the conflict didn't shift from Jablanica and Konjic to the area of Mostar. And then once that happened, it was not possible to communicate with Jablanica, because on the road, Your Honours, towards Jablanica and Konjic, this conflict in Mostar effected, in fact, a break in the communication.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bagaric, when you say you treated both, you are talking about the HVO and the Croats and the Bosniaks; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So the units of the HVO who were there and the units of the Bosnia and Herzegovina Army who were in that area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I apologise. I am just saying this is the 6th of May, the 6th of May. This is after the conflict in Konjic and that part up there. Just one moment. This is very important. At that time, I think there were no more HVO soldiers in this hospital. All trust was lost, but still we did relieve that surgical team.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: My question referred to the time-period when this hospital was established.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, you are correct. Yes, you are correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Would you please look at P02221 [as interpreted]. The question will be short, because this is already an exhibit. On the 11th of May, 1993, an approval was given by Mr. Stojic for the transport of plasma for the hospital in Mostar. This is obviously the hospital in East Mostar. I'm asking you this: Can you confirm for the Trial Chamber that you were involved and that you were aware of plasma being sent to East Mostar and whether the date was also the 11th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: Blood did not go there that often as medicines and drugs, but I know for a fact that there was one such case when blood was indeed sent to the eastern side of Mostar. I don't know, I can't confirm that this was the case or whether there was another case. Maybe there were several such cases, but I wouldn't know. We simply did not have blood, and we had to borrow it from Split. I remember on two occasions we did it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And now follows a series of documents, starting with 2D119. This is a letter of yours dated 3rd June 1993, sent to the Command of the 4th Corps of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and could you please provide a brief comment?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: On the 3rd of June, it was aired on the radio that the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, i.e., the eastern side of Mostar after the conflict in the month of May - am I right in saying that it was in the month of May? Yes, it was - that they did not have any medicines and medical supplies, and then I did not sign this personally, it was signed by a colleague on my behalf, and then we sent the offer to the other side, saying that we had heard that they were lacking supplies and that we were awaiting for their breakdown to see if we could help them.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to correct a number in the transcript. Page number 84, line 15, the number should read "P02291." There are too many 2s. P02291 is the correct number. P02291; two 2s. Now it's correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Following the letter that we have just looked at under number 2D119, can we look at document 2D120?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Your brief comment, please. Does this document arise from the previous offer that you provided?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: Yes. The commander of the 4th Corps of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Arif Pasalic, replied to our offer and asked to -- actually, was taking us up on our -- taking us up on our offer and providing us with the list or the breakdown of everything they needed. I believe that some things are missing in the list, but, yes, it did happen, it did transpire after our letter. We're talking about a list of all the drugs and medicines.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you please look at 2D504?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The order issued by Mr. Tugomir Gveric is related to the previous request of the 4th Corps for the delivery of drugs?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is precisely that. After we had received the request from the 4th Corps, Mr. Gveric says, Drugs to be issued according to the breakdown enclosed, provided by the BiH Army, that quantities should be available within seven days.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you please look at 2D321 [Realtime transcript read in error, "2D201"] that's the next document in the series.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Again, this was signed by Tugomir Gveric on the 8th of June. Could you please tell us whether this is in relation to the request?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: I believe so. Not that I believe so; yes, I'm sure that that's the request.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bagaric, I apologise. What about the batch of drugs and medical supplies that was sent to the BiH Army; did it relate to the request by Mr. Arif Pasalic?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: I believe that I said yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to correct. On page 96, line 15, it should read "Document 2D321." That's the number of the document, 2D321.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is the document that you have just looked at?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you please now look at 3D634?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The date is 16 June. It was signed by Mr. Tugomir Gveric, and it says the Central Depot, Drugs and Medical Supplies of the HZ-HB, Supply for the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: That's correct, but I don't see here and I'm not sure whether that is the correct date. I'm not sure whether this is the 15th of May or the 16th of May. It was in Mostar, but this definitely refers to one and the same matter, I'm sure, I'm convinced.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I believe that this is obvious, that the date is 16th of May.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: I apologise. If this is the 16th of June, how can it say, in English "16th of May"?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bagaric, I asked you whether this was the same matter. We looked at the request, and now I'm asking you whether this is the same request, because the whole thing is not legible enough. That's why I'm asking, if Mr. Pasalic, in document 2D120, sent a request on the 5th of June, 1993. That's why I'm asking you whether the document covers the dispatch of medicines pursuant to that particular request.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you please now look at 2D122.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a new request dated 9 June. Could you please comment briefly upon this request?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: Well, nothing, this is precisely what I was talking about. He wants a passage -- safe passage to be provided for a shift of the surgical team, and the execution of a list of drugs, and then he mentions a vehicle, the one that somebody -- and he says "you had seized from me," and this is all. This is precisely that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Bagaric, is this a new request?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: Yeah, it's a new request, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you please look at 2D233?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a letter by Mr. Tugomir Gveric, who refers to the previous document in his answer, and he says: "As regards the request of the Command of the 4th Corps sent to the Main Medical Staff of the HVO, we are duty-bound to answer we are sending the medical equipment and drugs as per your request. We are waiting UNPROFOR transportation. As regards your request for an ambulance, we have to draw attention to the fact that during the aggression against the town of Mostar, you deliberately destroyed 19 ambulances, wounded 6 drivers and killed 1. We are not in a position to meet your request." The number of the document is so-and-so. 2D323. I apologise. My attention has been drawn to the error. Could you please comment? We're still talking about a team of doctors, specialists?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BAGARIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This is just a confirmation of what I have said a minute ago. Due to the conflict, all communication with the war hospital in Jablanica was discontinued, interrupted. Why was that? Because there is no dispute that drugs were sent, they were being sent at the time, and so on and so forth. However, my colleague Gveric says that we don't have any ambulances. That was a fact. At least we didn't have enough in order to be able to send them to others. And when it comes to surgical teams, we had volunteers among the doctors who were willing to go, and I know this for a fact, and I claim with full responsibility that nobody volunteered to go, be it Muslims or Croats, and we really could not, under such dire circumstances when we could not be guaranteed safety for these people, we could not send them, we could not force them to leave. We just could not send them with force to Jablanica. That's that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is 7.00. Maybe this would be a good time to adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now it's over 7.00. Ms. Nozica, you will have 50 minutes, roughly, tomorrow. Witness, you will come tomorrow afternoon, since we will resume at a quarter past 2.00 tomorrow. I wish everybody a pleasant evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 21st day of April, 2009, at 2.15 p.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
